target: Coitado, ele não merece isso.
english: Poor thing, he doesn't deserve that.
tip: 'Coitado/coitada' means 'poor thing.' Used to express sympathy. It's not rude – it's genuinely empathetic.

target: Ele soube a verdade ontem.
english: He found out the truth yesterday.
tip: 'Saber' past: ele soube. The past of 'saber' often means 'found out' – a completed discovery.

target: Nós almoçamos juntos na sexta passada.
english: We had lunch together last Friday.
tip: 'Almoçamos' is the same for present and past (nós form). Context tells you which tense: 'ontem almoçamos' = past, 'sempre almoçamos' = present.

target: Eu acordei com dor de cabeça.
english: I woke up with a headache.
tip: Regular -ar past: acordar → acordei. 'Dor de cabeça' = headache (literally 'pain of head').

target: Ele quis ajudar, mas não conseguiu.
english: He wanted to help, but couldn't.
tip: 'Querer' past: ele quis. 'Quis ajudar, mas não conseguiu' = wanted to help but couldn't.

target: Vamos combinar para a semana que vem.
english: Let's set something up for next week.
tip: 'Vamos + combinar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Ela vendeu o carro na semana passada.
english: She sold the car last week.
tip: Regular -er past: vender → vendeu (ela). Second conjugation past: drop -er, add -eu.

target: Eu corri cinco quilômetros hoje de manhã.
english: I ran five kilometers this morning.
tip: Regular -er past: correr → corri (eu). First person -er/-ir past: drop ending, add -i.

target: A gente cantou karaokê a noite inteira.
english: We sang karaoke all night long.
tip: Regular -ar past: cantar → cantou. 'A noite inteira' = the whole night. 'A gente cantou.'

target: Ele parou de fumar há seis meses.
english: He stopped smoking six months ago.
tip: 'Parar de' + infinitive means 'to stop doing something.' 'Há' + time means 'ago': 'há seis meses' = six months ago.

target: Ele fez questão de pagar o jantar.
english: He insisted on paying for dinner.
tip: 'Fazer' past: ele fez. 'Fazer questão de' = to insist on – a common fixed expression.

target: A gente chegou atrasado por causa do trânsito.
english: We arrived late because of traffic.
tip: Regular -ar past: chegar → chegou. With 'a gente,' always singular: 'a gente chegou.'

target: Pode deixar que eu resolvo.
english: Don't worry, I'll take care of it.
tip: 'Pode deixar' means 'leave it to me' or 'don't worry about it.' It's a very reassuring Brazilian expression.

target: Vocês foram ao show ontem?
english: Did you go to the concert yesterday?
tip: 'Ir' past: vocês foram. 'Foram' is past of both 'ir' and 'ser' – context tells which. Here: 'went.'

target: Eu perdi a carteira no ônibus.
english: I lost my wallet on the bus.
tip: Regular -er past: perder → perdi. First person: -i. 'Perder' = to lose. 'Carteira' = wallet.

target: Eu pus o dinheiro na carteira.
english: I put the money in my wallet.
tip: 'Pôr' past: eu pus. Very irregular: pôr → eu pus, ele pôs, nós pusemos. 'Na carteira' = in the wallet.

target: Eu liguei para você, mas não atendeu.
english: I called you, but you didn't answer.
tip: Regular -ar past: ligar → liguei. Note the spelling change: g → gu before -ei to keep the /g/ sound.

target: Eu mudei de ideia sobre a viagem.
english: I changed my mind about the trip.
tip: Regular -ar past: mudar → mudei. 'Mudar de ideia' = to change one's mind (fixed expression).

target: A gente quis ajudar, mas ela recusou.
english: We wanted to help, but she refused.
tip: 'Querer' → 'quis' (I wanted/tried). In negative preterite: 'não quis' = refused.

target: Eu estava dormindo quando o telefone tocou.
english: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
tip: Classic past contrast: imperfeito sets the scene (was sleeping = ongoing), perfeito interrupts it (rang = sudden event).

target: Eu lavei toda a louça depois do jantar.
english: I washed all the dishes after dinner.
tip: Regular -ar past: lavar → lavei. 'Toda a louça' = all the dishes. 'Depois do' = after the.

target: Senta aí, faz de conta que é da casa.
english: Sit down, act like you're at home.
tip: 'Fazer de conta' means 'to pretend.' 'Faz de conta que é da casa' is a warm invitation to feel comfortable.

target: Ela perguntou se eu queria ir junto.
english: She asked if I wanted to go along.
tip: Regular -ar past: perguntar → perguntou. 'Se' introduces indirect questions: 'perguntou se eu queria.'

target: Nós arrumamos a sala para a festa.
english: We set up the room for the party.
tip: Regular -ar past: arrumar → arrumamos. 'Arrumar' = to tidy up/arrange. 'Para a festa' = for the party.

target: Ela comprou um vestido novo para a festa.
english: She bought a new dress for the party.
tip: Regular -ar past: comprar → comprou (ele/ela). Third person singular: drop -ar, add -ou.

target: Nós estávamos com fome quando encontramos o restaurante.
english: We were hungry when we found the restaurant.
tip: 'está' (estar) – marks a temporary condition, emotion, or location. Ser would imply permanence.

target: Faz tempo que não nos vemos.
english: It's been a while since we've seen each other.
tip: 'nos' contracts em+os – mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: Que pena, eu não vou poder ir.
english: What a shame, I won't be able to go.
tip: 'Que pena' means 'what a shame/pity.' Very common for expressing regret or disappointment.

target: Ela fez uma viagem incrível para Fernando de Noronha.
english: She took an incredible trip to Fernando de Noronha.
tip: 'Fazer' past: ela fez. 'Fez uma viagem' = took a trip. 'Fazer viagem' is the natural expression.

target: Eu bebi muita água de coco na praia.
english: I drank a lot of coconut water at the beach.
tip: Regular -er past: beber → bebi. 'Água de coco' = coconut water – a beloved Brazilian drink.

target: Pega leve, ele está passando por um momento difícil.
english: Go easy on him, he's going through a tough time.
tip: 'Pegar leve' means 'to go easy on' or 'to take it easy.' The opposite is 'pegar pesado' (to be harsh/to overdo it).

target: Eu sempre almoçava em casa, mas hoje almocei no restaurante.
english: I always used to eat lunch at home, but today I ate at the restaurant.
tip: 'Almoçava' (imperfeito, habitual) + 'almocei' (perfeito, today's specific event). Habit vs. single action.

target: Eu sempre tomava café às sete, mas ontem tomei às oito.
english: I always used to have coffee at seven, but yesterday I had it at eight.
tip: Imperfeito for habitual routine (tomava = used to), perfeito for a specific one-time event (tomei = I had, just once).

target: A gente torceu para o Flamengo.
english: We cheered for Flamengo.
tip: 'Torcer para' means to root for/cheer for a team. Flamengo is Brazil's most popular soccer team, with fans across the entire country.

target: Vocês aproveitaram as férias?
english: Did you enjoy the vacation?
tip: Regular -ar past: aproveitar → aproveitaram. 'Aproveitar' = to enjoy/take advantage of.

target: Vocês visitaram o museu?
english: Did you visit the museum?
tip: Regular -ar past: visitar → visitaram. 'O museu' = the museum (masculine noun).

target: Vocês provaram a feijoada?
english: Did you try the feijoada?
tip: Feijoada is Brazil's national dish – a rich black bean stew with pork. Traditionally served on Wednesdays and Saturdays.

target: Vocês receberam o meu e-mail?
english: Did you receive my email?
tip: Regular -er past: receber → receberam (vocês). Second conjugation plural past: -eram.

target: Ele começou um curso de inglês.
english: He started an English course.
tip: Regular -ar past: começar → começou. Spelling change: ç stays before -ou (no change needed here).

target: A gente curtiu muito a praia.
english: We really enjoyed the beach.
tip: 'Curtir' means to enjoy/have fun. In the past: 'curti a festa' = I enjoyed the party. Very common in informal Brazilian Portuguese.

target: Nós caminhamos pela orla da praia.
english: We walked along the beachfront.
tip: Regular -ar past: caminhar → caminhamos. 'Pela orla' = por + a = along the waterfront.

target: Eu resolvi o problema do computador.
english: I fixed the computer problem.
tip: Regular -er past: resolver → resolvi. 'Resolver' = to solve/fix. Very common in daily Brazilian Portuguese.

target: A gente pulou Carnaval no Rio.
english: We skipped Carnival in Rio.
tip: 'Pular Carnaval' is the Brazilian expression for celebrating/partying during Carnival. Literally 'to jump Carnival.'

target: Ela quis ir embora mais cedo.
english: She wanted to leave earlier.
tip: 'Querer' in the past: quis, quis, quisemos, quiseram. Completely irregular – the stem changes to 'quis-.'

target: A gente alugou uma casa na praia.
english: We rented a beach house.
tip: Regular -ar past: alugar → alugou. 'A gente alugou' – remember singular conjugation with 'a gente.'

target: A gente dançou forró a noite inteira.
english: We danced forró all night.
tip: The pretérito perfeito captures a specific past event – 'dançou' tells us the dancing happened at a defined moment.

target: Ele terminou o relatório a tempo.
english: He finished the report on time.
tip: Regular -ar past: terminar → terminou. 'A tempo' = on time (just in time). 'No prazo' = by the deadline.

target: A gente passeou pelo centro histórico.
english: We strolled through the historic center.
tip: Regular -ar past: passear → passeou. 'Pelo centro' = por + o = through/around the center.

target: Nós dividimos a pizza entre quatro.
english: We split the pizza among four.
tip: Regular -ir past: dividir → dividimos. Same as present form – past meaning clear from 'pizza entre quatro.'

target: Ele entregou o projeto no prazo.
english: He delivered the project on time.
tip: Regular -ar past: entregar → entregou. 'No prazo' = on time/by the deadline.

target: Nós tivemos uma reunião longa hoje.
english: We had a long meeting today.
tip: 'Ter' in the past: tive, teve, tivemos, tiveram. Completely irregular – no pattern to follow, just memorize.

target: Vocês sabiam que ela era brasileira?
english: Did you know she was Brazilian?
tip: 'Se' can mark reciprocity with plural subjects: 'Eles se abraçaram' (They hugged each other).

target: Ela fez um bolo de chocolate incrível.
english: She made an incredible chocolate cake.
tip: 'Fazer' is irregular in the past: fiz, fez, fizemos, fizeram. 'Fez' is one of the most common past tense forms you'll hear.

target: A gente fez amizade com os vizinhos.
english: We became friends with the neighbors.
tip: 'Fazer' past: a gente fez. 'Fazer amizade com' = to become friends with – a useful expression.

target: Ele deu um abraço apertado em todo mundo.
english: He gave everyone a tight hug.
tip: 'Dar' → 'dei, deu, demos, deram.' Despite being -ar, it takes irregular endings.

target: Eu comi muito no churrasco.
english: I ate a lot at the barbecue.
tip: Regular -er verbs in the past: -i, -eu, -emos, -eram. 'Comer' → 'comi' (eu), 'comeu' (ele/ela).

target: Vocês experimentaram o açaí daqui?
english: Did you try the açaí from here?
tip: Regular -ar past: experimentar → experimentaram. 'Experimentar' = to try (food/experience). 'O açaí daqui' = the açaí from here.

target: Minha avó cozinhava muito bem.
english: My grandmother used to cook very well.
tip: Imperfeito of -ar: cozinhava (avó). Describes a habitual ability in the past – grandma used to cook well.

target: Eu fui ao médico na terça-feira.
english: I went to the doctor on Tuesday.
tip: 'Ir' and 'ser' share the same past tense forms: fui, foi, fomos, foram. Context tells you which verb it is: 'fui ao médico' = I went.

target: Nós viemos de taxi porque choveu.
english: We came by taxi because it rained.
tip: 'Vir' past: nós viemos. Don't confuse 'viemos' (came) with 'vimos' (saw). 'De taxi' = by taxi.
